cells.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that for certain revenue-producing employees in its Wealth Management and Investment Management segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.quote: For certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.scope: Wealth Management and Investment Management segments

items.text: Morgan Stanley attributes increased compensation and benefits expenses in part to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors on higher revenues/compensable revenue.
items.quote: Compensation and benefits expenses of $29,216 million in 2025 increased 12% from the prior year, primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors and higher discretionary incentive compensation within Institutional Securities, both on higher revenues, and higher salary expenses.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it will increase the cash component of its advisor compensation and that it is transitioning all economic hedges for deferred cash-based compensation (DCP) obligations to derivative instruments.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. We are making these changes to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings.

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that the amount of the client fee is a factor used in calculating the compensation paid to the Financial Advisor, and that if the fee rate is below a certain threshold the advisor is given credit for less than the total fee, giving advisors a financial incentive not to reduce fees below that threshold.
items.quote: The amount of the fee you pay is a factor we use in calculating the compensation we pay your Financial Advisor. ... If your fee rate is below a certain threshold, we give your Financial Advisor credit for less than the total amount of your fee in calculating his or her compensation.

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor (MSVA) is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.
items.quote: If your account is serviced through a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor ("MSVA"), your MSVA is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that a portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee is paid to the client's Financial Advisor.
items.quote: A portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee will be paid to your Financial Advisor.

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that Financial Advisors and their Branch Managers receive no additional compensation as a result of certain payments (brokerage commissions, revenue-sharing, administrative service fees, expense reimbursement and data analytics fees) received by Morgan Stanley from certain Funds.
items.quote: Financial Advisors and their Branch Managers receive no additional compensation as a result of these payments received by Morgan Stanley.

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that Financial Advisors in advisory programs do not receive additional compensation as a result of revenue sharing support fees, mutual fund administrative service fees and data analytics payments received by Morgan Stanley.
items.quote: To mitigate these conflicts, Financial Advisors in advisory programs do not receive additional compensation as a result of the support fees, mutual fund administrative service fees and data analytics payments received by Morgan Stanley.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation, requiring advisors to stay at the firm for years to vest (golden handcuffs).
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year; the firm is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its compensation programs (which vary by location) as including, in addition to salaries, annual bonuses, retirement savings plans with matching contributions, an employee stock purchase plan, student loan refinancing and a financial wellbeing program.
items.quote: In addition to salaries, these programs (which vary by location) include annual bonuses, retirement savings plans with matching contributions, an employee stock purchase plan, student loan refinancing and a financial wellbeing program.

cells.reason: The passages contain multiple direct disclosures of Morgan Stanley's advisor compensation structure, including formulaic payouts, deferred compensation, cash component, fee-based compensation factors, and the MSVA salary-plus-bonus structure.
